rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse recalls the creation of the whole plant kingdom, including trees, but mentions forage as one useful kind.
rows.anchor: تذكير لخلق جنس النبات من شجر وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bringing out the pasture means bringing it forth from the earth by making it grow.
rows.anchor: إخراجه من الأرض وهو إنباته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-marʿā is vegetation grazed by livestock; it can be a place-name for grazing or a verbal noun used for the grazed object.
rows.anchor: الشيء المَرْعِيّ من إطلاق المصدر على المفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Choosing pasture rather than the general word plant evokes livestock’s benefit to people and preserves the verse ending.
rows.anchor: مادة الرعي من نفع الأنعام به ونفعها للناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception branches from “you forget”; mā is a relative pronoun, with “that God wills you to forget” understood.
rows.anchor: والاستثناء في قوله :  { إلا ما شاء الله }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception means that the Prophet may forget some revealed Quran if God wills it; Ibn ʿĀshūr distinguishes two kinds.
rows.anchor: أن بعض القرآن ينساه النبي إذا شاء الله أن ينساه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The more apparent kind is divinely ordered abrogation of recitation: the Prophet and Muslims cease reciting the passage until they forget it.
rows.anchor: وهو أظهرهما أن الله إذا شاء نسخ تلاوة بعض ما أنزل

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: ʿUmar reported that the stoning passage and a warning against disavowing one’s fathers had once been revealed and recited.
rows.anchor: ما روي عن عمر أنه قال :  « كان فيما أنزل الشيخُ والشيخه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr connects this abrogation of recitation with the reading “or cause it to be forgotten” in al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: وهذا ما أشير إليه بقوله تعالى :  { أو ننسها }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other kind is temporary human lapse in the Prophet’s memory, after which God provides a reminder.
rows.anchor: ما يعرض نسيانه للنبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم نسياناً موقتاً كشأن عوارض

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: In a report in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, ʿĀʾisha says a nighttime recitation by a man reminded the Prophet of verses he had omitted or forgotten.
rows.anchor: ففي « صحيح البخاري » عن عائشة قالت :  « سمع النبيءُ صلى الله عليه وسلم رجلاً

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Another Bukhārī report says Ubayy ibn Kaʿb asked whether a verse omitted in prayer had been abrogated; the Prophet replied, “I forgot it.”
rows.anchor: وفيه أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أسقط آية في قراءته في الصلاة فسأله أبي بن كعب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “You will not forget” is not a prohibition, since involuntary forgetting is outside legal duty; treating lā as prohibitive strains the explanation of its written alif.
rows.anchor: وليس قوله :  { فلا تنسى } من الخبر المستعمل في النهي عن النسيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about God knowing what is manifest and hidden is parenthetical and explains the promise that the Quran will be preserved from accidental loss.
rows.anchor: وجملة :  { إنه يعلم الجهر وما يخفى } معترضة وهي تعليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s spoken recitation is manifest to God, while a forgotten verse is hidden in memory and fails to emerge in speech, yet God knows it.
rows.anchor: ومناسبة الجهر وما يخفى أن ما يقرؤه الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم من القرآن هو من قبيل الجهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause is joined to the promise in verse 6, while verse 7 is parenthetical; the new promise broadens the result from preservation to enabling good.
rows.anchor: عطف على { سنقرئك فلا تنسى } [ الأعلى :  6 ]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taysīr means making an action easy for the person who performs it.
rows.anchor: جعل العمل يسيراً على عامله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of making easy is the thing facilitated; the beneficiary or purpose is expressed with a following lām, as in Moses’ prayer.
rows.anchor: ومفعول فعل التيسير هو الشيء الذي يُجعل يسيراً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-yusrā is the feminine of al-aysar; the fuʿlā form intensifies the quality because it is the feminine of an elative.
rows.anchor: مؤنث الأيسر ،  وصيغة فُعلى تدل على قوة الوصف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The described noun is omitted; its feminine adjective implies a feminine singular noun or a plural treated grammatically as feminine.
rows.anchor: تأنيث الوصف مشعر بأن الموصوف المحذوف مما يجري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The context points to the omitted noun being the religious law: the Messenger’s defining first responsibility is the law he was sent to deliver.
rows.anchor: وسياق الكلام الذي قبله يهدي إلى أن يكون الموصوف المقدر معنى الشريعة فإن خطاب الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the surface reading followed by the commentators, making the Prophet easy for the way means preparing and empowering him for easier religious duties and their good outcomes.
rows.anchor: إن حمل على ظاهر نظم الكلام وهو ما جرى عليه المفسرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God prepares the Prophet for ease in religion, including preserving the Quran, carrying the revealed law, and receiving worldly and afterlife good.
rows.anchor: أي نهيئك للأمور اليسرى في أمر الدين وعواقبه من تيسير حفظ القرآن لك وتيسير الشريعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām gives a purpose or end: God enables the Prophet for the way of ease and its acceptance.
rows.anchor: العلةُ ،  أي لأجل اليسرى ،  أي لقبولها

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet’s saying that everyone is enabled for what they were created for illustrates this sense and parallels the two outcomes in al-Layl.
rows.anchor: ونحوه قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the wording may use rhetorical inversion for “We make the easy way easy for you,” leaving the verb’s ordinary sense intact.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يجعل الكلام جاريا على خلاف مقتضى الظاهر بسلوك أسلوب القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the way “easy” suggests its ease is already established; God need only protect the Prophet from obstacles to receiving it.
rows.anchor: إيماء إلى استتباب تيسره لها بما أنها جُعلت يسرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise includes two forms of facilitation: making the Prophet’s charge easy while fulfilling its purpose, and enabling the Prophet to carry it out.
rows.anchor: تيسير ما كلف به النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أي جعله يسيراً مع وفائه بالمقصود منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inversion emphatically identifies the facilitated person with the facilitated way; Ibn ʿĀshūr cites the Arabic expression about presenting a camel to a trough, al-ʿAjjāj’s verse, and the Quranic image in al-Qaṣaṣ.
rows.anchor: بأن فيه تنزيل الشيء الميسر منزلة الشيء الميسر له والعكس للمبالغة في ثبوت الفعل للمفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse reassures the initially anxious Messenger that God equips him to bear the burdens of revelation and the demanding work of guiding the community.
rows.anchor: وعد الله إياه بأنه يسره لتلقي أعباء الرسالة فلا تشق عليه ولا تحرجه

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet’s preference for the easier of two options and his instruction that his companions were sent to facilitate, not make things difficult, exemplify this promise.
rows.anchor: ومن آثار هذا التيسير ما ورد في الحديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Whoever fears” denotes a whole class, not a particular person; the verb’s singular agreement follows the singular form of man.
rows.anchor: جنس لا فرد معين أي سيتذكر الذين يخشون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb is treated as intransitive: those whose disposition includes fear anticipate harm and benefit, investigate their sources, and ponder the evidence lest the warning apply to them.
rows.anchor: منزلة اللازم فلم يقدر له مفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khashya means fear, as in Ṭā Hā; fear has degrees, and believers differ according to their share of it.
rows.anchor: الخوف ، وتقدم في قوله تعالى :  { لعله يتذكر أو يخشى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tajannub means moving away; its form evokes taking a position at the side of something, figuratively seeking distance from it.
rows.anchor: وأصله تفعل لتكلف الكينونة بجانببٍ من شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article marks a class, so al-ashqā means the most wretched people generally.
rows.anchor: تعريف الجنس ، أي الأشقونْ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In religious usage, wretchedness is the afterlife state of humiliation and torment arising from unbelief; one who dies a believer is not wretched.
rows.anchor: والشقوة والشقاء في لسان الشرع الحالة الناشئة في الآخرة عن الكفر من حالة الإهانة والتعذيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr takes al-ashqā to mean the unbeliever, the most wretched because of eternal residence in Hell, including all polytheists.
rows.anchor: هو الكافر لأنه أشدّ الناس شقاء في الآخرة لخلوده في النار

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some commentators instead take the definite description as referring specifically to al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra or ʿUtba ibn Rabīʿa.
rows.anchor: ومن المفسرين من حمله على العهد فقال :  أريد به الوليد بن المغيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following description, “the one who enters the greatest Fire,” clarifies the otherwise ambiguous “most wretched” for the early audience.
rows.anchor: ووصف { الأشقى } ب { الذي يصلى النار الكبرى } لأن إطلاق { الأشقى } في هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast implies that the most wretched do not fear: absorbed in delusion and pleasure, they make no effort to escape their misery.
rows.anchor: ومقابلة { من يخشى } ب { الأشقى } تؤذن بأن { الأشقى } من شأنه

words: ثُمَّ لَا يَمُوتُ فِيهَا وَلَا يَحْيَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause is coordinated with “he enters the greatest Fire” as a second description of those who suffer there.
rows.anchor: عطف على جملة { يصلى النار الكبرى } فهي صلة ثانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thumma marks a rise in rank of severity: torment is worse when burning brings neither relief through death nor release through life.
rows.anchor: للتراخي الرتبي تدل على أن معطوفها متراخي الرتبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “He does not die” means sensation does not cease; the extraordinary state strengthens the image of the punishment.
rows.anchor: لا يزول عنه الإحساس ، فإن الموت فقدان الإحساس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The added denial of life prevents hearers from mistaking survival of the burning for painless or comfortable life; it means no life free of pain.
rows.anchor: احتراس لدفع توهم أن يراد بنفي الموت عنهم أنهم استراحوا من العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, denying life is a metonym for denying escape, since burning ordinarily entails death while life entails not dying.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن نجعل نفي الحياة كناية عن نفي الخلاص بناء على أن لازم الإحراق الهلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects reading the paired denials as merely a middle state between life and death, like “neither eastern nor western” or the saying about heat and cold.
rows.anchor: وليس هذا من قبيل نفي وصفين لإثبات حالةٍ وسطٍ بينَ حالتيهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse uses antithesis between dying and living.
rows.anchor: مُحسِّن الطباق لأجل التضاد الظاهر بين { لا يموت } و { لا يحيى }

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read the verb with second-person tāʾ, directly addressing the polytheists in the context and shifting from third person.
rows.anchor: قرأ الجمهور { تؤثرون } بمثناة فوقية بصيغة الخطاب

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr alone reads with third-person yāʾ, referring back to the most wretched person entering the Fire.
rows.anchor: وقرأه أبو عمرو وحده بالمثناة التحتية على طريقة الغيبة عائدا إلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bal has the general sense of turning to what follows; with single words it cancels the previous item or qualifies it.
rows.anchor: معناه الجامع هو الإضراب ، أي انصراف القول أو الحكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Between sentences, bal joins one utterance to another without necessarily sharing or reversing its judgment; it can either cancel the prior meaning or simply shift topics.
rows.anchor: وإذا عطف الجمل فعطفه عطف كلام على كلام وهو عطف لفظي مجرد عن التشريك في الحكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cancelling use is illustrated by the denial of the claim that the Prophet is possessed, followed by “rather, he brought them the truth.”
rows.anchor: نحو قوله تعالى :  { أم يقولون به جنة بل جاءهم بالحق }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The non-cancelling use merely moves from one report to another, as when the text shifts from a just record to hearts being heedless.
rows.anchor: نحو قوله تعالى :  { ولدينا كتاب ينطق بالحق وهم لا يظلمون بل قلوبهم في غمرة من هذا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here bal may simply move from those who benefit from or avoid the reminder to the reason the wretched avoid it: they prefer worldly life; this is especially clear on Abū ʿAmr’s reading.
rows.anchor: و { بل } هنا عاطفة جملة عطفاً صُورياً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the majority reading, bal shifts from narrating the two groups to rebuking the wretched directly, using an address shift to renew the listener’s attention.
rows.anchor: وأما على قراءة الجمهور فهو إضراب عن حكاية أحوال الفريقين بالانتقال إلى توبيخ أحد الفريقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, bal cancels the implication in “successful is whoever purifies” that the wretched might pursue success and join the God-fearing.
rows.anchor: لما تضمنه قوله :  { قد أفلح من تزكى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Īthār is choosing one thing from among several; here it means giving worldly life one’s attention and concern.
rows.anchor: تؤثرون الحياة الدنيا بعنايتكم واهتمامكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison is left unstated because the world implies the alternative: polytheists ignore any life beyond the present and dismiss reminders of the hereafter.
rows.anchor: ولم يذكر المؤثر عليه لأن الحياة الدنيا تدل عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This preference is the object of rebuke because the polytheists disbelieve in the hereafter and refuse to listen when it is described to them.
rows.anchor: فالمشركون لا يؤمنون بالآخرة وإذا ذكروا بالحياة الآخرة وأخبروا بها لم يعيروا سمعهم ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers also receive this warning: its force matches how much someone neglects salvation for worldly gain that brings afterlife consequences under the law.
rows.anchor: للمؤمنين حظا من هذه الموعظة على طول الدهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pursuing abundant worldly benefits is not blameworthy if one does not neglect the means of salvation in the hereafter.
rows.anchor: فأما الاستكثار من منافع الدنيا مع عدم إهمال أسباب النجاة في الآخرة فذلك ميدان للهمم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The assertion that the hereafter is better and more lasting follows the rebuke, reinforcing it by showing what the audience has ignored.
rows.anchor: عطف على جملة التوبيخ عطف الخبر على الإنشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abqā is a comparative meaning longer in duration.
rows.anchor: اسم تفضيل ، أي أطول بقاء

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A hadith about keeping a garment to the ankles calls that practice more God-fearing and more lasting.
rows.anchor: في حديث النهي عن جر الإزار « وليكن إلى الكعبين فإنه أتقى وأبقى »

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is a concluding amplification that honors the teaching as enduring guidance from the books of Abraham and Moses; the emphatic particles address deniers.
rows.anchor: تذييل للكلام وتنويه به بأنه من الكلام النافع الثابت في كتب إبراهيم وموسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “This” refers to the teaching in verses 14–17, not the opening of the sūra through verse 13, whose meaning is not established in Abraham’s and Moses’ books.
rows.anchor: إلى مجموع قوله { قد أفلح من تزكى إلى قوله وأبقى }

rows.speaker: أبو ذر
rows.claim: Abū Dharr asked the Prophet whether anything from Abraham’s and Moses’ scrolls had been revealed to him; the Prophet answered with verses 14–17. Ibn ʿĀshūr could not assess the report’s grade.
rows.anchor: عن أبي ذر قال :  « قلت يا رسول الله هل أنزل عليك شيء مما كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “In the scrolls” means that equivalent content was written in them; the container stands metonymically for what it contains, as in the reference to one’s record.
rows.anchor: أن مماثله في المعنى مكتوب في الصحف الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣuḥuf is a nonstandard plural of ṣaḥīfa, but more eloquent than the regular ṣaḥāʾif, like sufُن for safīna.
rows.anchor: جمع صحيفة على غير قياس لأن قياس جمعه صحائف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural fits because Abraham had scrolls and Moses had many, collectively represented by the scrolls of the Torah books.
rows.anchor: ووجه جمع الصحف أن إبراهيم كانت له صحف وأن موسى كانت له صحف كثيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording uses summary followed by detail to reinforce the claim: “the scrolls of Abraham and Moses” apposes “the earlier scrolls.”
rows.anchor: وجاء نظم الكلام على أسلوب الإجمال والتفصيل ليكون لهذا الخبر مزيد تقرير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ūlā is a feminine adjective for the broken plural ṣuḥuf, which is treated as feminine.
rows.anchor: و { الأولى } : وصف لصحف الذي هو جمع تكسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr reports three analyses for the roots and form of awwal: hamza-wāw-lām, wāw-wāw-lām with an added hamza, or wāw-hamza-lām with metathesis; ūlā’s derivation varies accordingly.
rows.anchor: واختلف في الحروف الأصلية للفظ أول فقيل : حروفه الأصول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Earlier” means earlier than the Quran, not the first scriptures ever, since some messengers before Abraham reportedly received scrolls.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالأولية في وصف الصحف سبق الزمان بالنسبة إلى القرآن لا التي لم يسبقها غيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Bukhārī hadith calls “if you feel no shame, do as you wish” a saying preserved from the earliest prophecy.
rows.anchor: إنَّ مما أدرك الناسُ من كلام النبوءة الأولى

rows.speaker: أبو ذر
rows.claim: Abū Dharr reports from the Prophet that Abraham’s scrolls numbered ten; Ibn ʿĀshūr names the transmitters but gives no grade.
rows.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد وابن مردويه وابن عساكر وأبو بكر الآجري عن أبي ذر عن رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause “you are not a controller over them” is an appositive elaboration of the negative side of the preceding restriction.
rows.anchor: بدل اشتمال من جملة القصر باعتبار جانب النفي الذي يفيده القصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muṣayṭir means one who compels or coerces; ṣayṭara also occurs with initial sīn, though ṣād is more common.
rows.anchor: يقال : صيطر بصاد في أوله ، ويقال : سيطر بسين في أوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word appeared in al-Ṭūr as well; Ibn ʿĀshūr notes the different recitations there and here.
rows.anchor: وتقدم في سورة الطور ( 37 ) : { أم هم المصيطرون }

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read the word with initial ṣād.
rows.anchor: وقرأ بها الجمهور

rows.speaker: هشام عن ابن عامر
rows.claim: Hishām, transmitting from Ibn ʿĀmir, reads it with initial sīn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ هشام عن ابن عامر بالسين

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Ḥamza reads with ṣād pronounced with a zāy-like quality.
rows.anchor: وقرأه حمزة بإشمام الصاد صوت الزاي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The negative statement reassures the Prophet that he is not accountable for their continued disbelief, since he was not charged with coercing them into faith.
rows.anchor: فالخبر بهذا النفي مستعمل كناية عن التطمين برفع التبعة عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr rejects abrogation by fighting verses: combat became obligatory after a sequence of aggressions initiated by polytheists, including expelling Muslims, to secure them from oppression.
rows.anchor: ثم جاء وجوب القتال بتسلسل حوادث كان المشركون هم البادئين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects using this verse as a guarantee of religious freedom within the Muslim community, distinguishing that setting from relations with polytheists.
rows.anchor: ومن الجهلة من يضع قوله :  { لست عليهم بمصيطر } في غير موضعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He states that an apostate is asked to repent for three days and killed if unrepentant; if unavailable, Muslims must expel and treat the person as a combatant.
rows.anchor: فمن يلحد في الإسلام بعد الدخول فيه يستتاب ثلاثاً فإن لم يتب قتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He applies the same rule to a person who renounces Islam or denies a necessary tenet after its implication is explained, then persists without an acceptable interpretation or desisting.
rows.anchor: وكذلك من جاء بقول أو عمل يقتضي نبذ الإسلام أو إنكار ما هو من أصول الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object “over them” precedes its complement “controller” to preserve the verse ending.
rows.anchor: وتقديم { عليهم } على متعلقه وهو « مسيطر » للرعاية على الفاصلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Hell was brought” is like saying a king arrived: Hell is brought into view and its gates opened, as in two other Quranic descriptions.
rows.anchor: واستعمال { وجيء يومئذ بجهنم } كاستعمال مَجيء الملك

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: A Muslim report from Ibn Masʿūd, raised to the Prophet, says Hell has 70,000 reins, each drawn by 70,000 angels; the report glosses its being brought, and afterlife events transcend custom.
rows.anchor: وورد في حديث مسلم عن ابن مسعود يرفعه :  « أن لجهنم سبعين ألف زمام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only Hell is mentioned because the sūra warns those who failed to remember; Paradise too will be brought near, as another verse says.
rows.anchor: وإنما اقتصر على ذكر جهنم لأن المقصود في هذه السورة وعيد الذين لم يتذكروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first “that day” modifies “was brought”; the implied day is when the earth is crushed repeatedly, continuing the preceding context.
rows.anchor: والتقدير : وجيء يوم تدك الأرض دكاً دكاً إلى آخره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second “that day” apposes the earlier “when the earth is crushed”; both expressions are governed by “remember.”
rows.anchor: و { يومئذ } الثاني بدل من { إذا دكت الأرض } والمعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The time phrase is advanced for emphasis and suspense; summary then detail and its repetition reconnect the clause after a long interruption.
rows.anchor: وتقديمه للاهتمام مع ما في الإطناب من التشويق ليحصل الإجمال ثم التفصيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The human” means the unbeliever from the person described in verse 15; the noun is repeated instead of a pronoun because its antecedent is distant.
rows.anchor: وهو الذي تقدم ذكره في قوله تعالى : { فأما الإنسان إذا ما ابتلاه ربه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parenthetical question interrupts between remembering and speaking; annā means “where,” and the rhetorical question denies any benefit from belated recollection, with “benefit” omitted.
rows.anchor: معترضة بين جملة { يتذكر الإنسان } وجملة : { يقول } الخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance literally means showing the route to the destination one intends to reach; najd is elevated ground below a mountain.
rows.anchor: والهداية : الدلالة على الطريق المبلغة إلى المكان المقصود السير إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance is metaphorical inspiration to discern harm from benefit, the basis of human civilization and knowledge, and guidance through Islam to salvation.
rows.anchor: وقد استعيرت الهداية هنا للإلهام الذي جعله الله في الإنسان يدرك به الضار والنافع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two elevated paths symbolize good and evil: good is hard to follow, while evil is hard in its consequences, foreshadowing the next verse’s steep ascent.
rows.anchor: واستعير النجدان للخير والشر ، وجعلا نجدين لصعوبة اتباع أحدهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The image also compares thought toward a goal to travel along a road; receiving Islam’s call likewise felt difficult to its audience, as another verse says people were shown the way.
rows.anchor: ويتضمن ذلك تشبيه إعمال الفكر لنوال المطلوب بالسير في الطريق الموصل إلى المكان المرغوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse also embeds gratitude to humanity for the means God granted for living rightly.
rows.anchor: وأدمج في هذا الاستدلال امتنان على الإنسان بما وهبه من وسائل العيش المستقيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, guidance may mean reason directing people to consider evidence for God’s existence and unity, from which reflection would disclose divine unity.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون الهداية هداية العقل للتفكير في دلائل وجود الله ووحدانيته بحيث لو تأمل لعرف وحدانية الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This reading supports accountability for shirk and atheism during periods without messengers under one position in the dispute between Ashʿarites and Māturīdīs/Muʿtazilites.
rows.anchor: يكون هذا دليلا على سبب مؤاخذة أهل الشرك والتعطيل بكفرهم في أزمان الخلو عن إرسال الرسل
